transcript.prompt: I do digital forensics. Give me the landscape: when you receive a disk image from an incident, how do you approach browser artefacts as evidence?
transcript.response:
Browser artefacts ≠ “History file.” Treat them as a **constellation** of DBs, caches, key bags, and OS corroboration. Disk image = dead-box. That already changes what you can prove.

1) Intake (before any parse)
- Hash image. Mount RO. ⊥ write to evidence.
- Copy whole profile dirs, not single files. SQLite needs `-wal` `-shm` `-journal` or you lose uncheckpointed rows.
- Record OS, users, TZ, browser **version/build**. Schema + encryption model depend on it.
- Find **all** containers: every OS user, every Chromium profile (`Default`, `Profile 1`, Guest), Firefox random profile IDs, Safari, portable/Tor, **Electron/WebView2** (Slack/Teams/Discord = same artefact shapes).
- `Local State` → `profile.info_cache` = profile inventory + which Google/MS account signed in.
- Sync on → some visits may originate on another device. Attribution ! local-only.

2) What lives where (Chromium family = Chrome/Edge/Brave/Opera/Vivaldi/Arc)

Windows:
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\`
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\`
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\BraveSoftware\Brave-Browser\User Data\`

Linux:
`~/.config/google-chrome/`  `~/.config/microsoft-edge/`  `~/.mozilla/firefox/`

macOS:
`~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/`
`~/Library/Safari/`

High-value files:

| Store | Proves | Caveat |
|---|---|---|
| `History` | URLs, visit times, transition type, downloads, typed/search terms | Prefetch/redirect ≠ “user clicked this” |
| `Network/Cookies` | session existence, last_access, host | values often encrypted; last_access ≠ page visit |
| `Login Data` | saved-account **metadata** (origin, username, dates, use count) | password blob encrypted |
| `Web Data` | autofill, addresses, card metadata | same |
| `Bookmarks` JSON | intent / persistence | weak on timing |
| `Preferences` + extensions | config, malicious add-ons, enterprise policy | |
| `Local State` | AES key bag (`os_crypt.encrypted_key`), profile list | key to decrypt cookies/passwords |
| `Sessions/` Current+Last | open tabs at last clean shutdown | overwrite-prone |
| Cache / Code Cache | **page bodies** (phishing HTML, images) | high churn |
| Local Storage / IndexedDB (LevelDB) | SaaS tokens, web-app state | parser-hard; case gold |
| Network Action Predictor / Shortcuts / Top Sites | typed intent, even if URL never committed | survives some clears |
| `Media History` | played audio/video URLs | |
| Favicons | weak support only | ⊥ standalone visit proof |

Firefox: `places.sqlite` (history+bookmarks), `cookies.sqlite`, `formhistory.sqlite`, `logins.json`+`key4.db`, `sessionstore.jsonlz4`, `cache2/`, `storage/`, `extensions.json`.
Safari: `History.db`, `Downloads.plist`, `Cookies.binarycookies`, `Bookmarks.plist`, `LastSession.plist`. Tombstones in Safari history = direct delete evidence.

3) Epochs (wrong conversion = wrong case)
- Chromium: WebKit µs since 1601-01-01 UTC
- Firefox: PRTime µs since 1970-01-01 UTC
- Safari: Cocoa seconds since 2001-01-01 UTC → unix = cocoa + 978307200
Always store UTC. Validate vs a known event (download file on disk, meeting, proxy log).

4) Dead image vs live — 2024+ wall
Chrome/Edge **127+** App-Bound Encryption (ABE): cookie/password keys bound to signed `chrome.exe` via Elevation Service.
Dead-box + user password **used to** unwrap DPAPI. Now often **does not**. Offline you still get History, downloads, bookmarks, extensions, cache, visit metadata, cookie **names/hosts/times**. Plaintext cookie values / saved passwords frequently stay blobs.
Firefox / old Chromium: dead-box decrypt still often possible with OS key material.
If box still live and cookies/sessions in scope → live triage **before** pull-plug. Image still needed; live is additive, not a substitute.

Decrypt bundle (Windows, pre-ABE / where ABE not in play): `Cookies` + `Login Data` + `Local State` + DPAPI master keys under `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Protect\`. Metadata useful even if you never unwrap. Stay inside warrant/scope. Session replay into live accounts = access, not parsing — don’t do it without explicit authority.

5) Approach order on the image
1. Inventory browsers/profiles/versions/sync.
2. Stage copies. Open copies only.
3. Parse `History` + downloads first (unencrypted, highest yield).
4. Cookie **metadata** + login **metadata** (who they had accounts with).
5. Cache → actual content seen (phish pages).
6. Web storage → webmail/SaaS/chat web clients.
7. Extensions → persistence / infostealer / proxy add-ons.
8. Integrity: visit-id gaps, Safari tombstones, WAL/freelist carve, “Clear data” residue (Top Sites, NAP, `-wal`).
9. Unified timeline vs OS: `$MFT`, Prefetch, UserAssist, JumpLists, SRUM, EVTX, DNS, proxy/EDR.
10. Hypothesis-test. Don’t narrate a story the artefacts don’t carry.

6) What “Clear” / Incognito / Tor actually do
- Clear History = SQL DELETE (+ maybe VACUUM), not wipe. WAL, freelist, cache unlinks, NAP, Top Sites, Prefetch, DNS often remain. SSD TRIM eats slack fast.
- Incognito: little **in-profile**. Residues: RAM, `pagefile.sys`/`hiberfil.sys`, DNS cache (live), Prefetch/UserAssist (browser launched), gateway/proxy/ISP. Textbook “zero trace” is false **system-wide**, true-ish **in the profile**.
- Tor: treat as near-empty on disk by design. Look outside the profile.
- Private ≠ portable ≠ normal. Portable browsers leave profiles in odd paths — sweep, don’t assume `%LOCALAPPDATA%`.

7) Interpretation traps
- `transition` types: typed vs link vs generated vs reload vs keyword. Generated/prefetch ≠ intent.
- Sync + multiple profiles + shared family PC → “this URL on this disk” ≠ “this human typed it.”
- Cookie for a domain + no history row still possible (embed, clear, private).
- Download row without file on disk (deleted, failed, different volume).
- Favicon / GPUCache / Code Cache = usage smell, not proof of visit.

8) Tooling (examiner, RO copies)
- Parse/timeline: Hindsight (`pyhindsight`), Plaso, Autopsy, Magnet/FTK/AXIOM.
- Targeted: NirSoft ChromeCacheView / BrowsingHistoryView, DB Browser for SQLite, KAPE browser targets.
- Newer FOSS: `webx` (acquiredsecurity/forensic-webhistory), `br4n6` (browser-forensic) — WAL/freelist carve, Electron sweep.
- ⊥ open original DBs in a live browser. That mutates WAL and last-access.

9) Report like an examiner
State: source path, hash, browser+build, profile, epoch conversion, whether values were encrypted, what was **not** recoverable (ABE, TRIM, private). Separate **observation** from **inference**. Correlate ≥2 independent artefacts before you call a visit “user-driven.”

Want next: Chromium `History` schema cheat-sheet (visits/transition bits) or a KAPE/Hindsight triage checklist for Windows images.

transcript.prompt: Now the architecture of a forensics pass over a mounted image: artefact discovery, extraction, and reporting, with chain-of-custody in mind.
transcript.response:
Architecture of one pass over a **mounted image**. Original image stays sealed. Everything below runs on a RO mount + hashed working copies.

0) Evidence object (never mutate)
```
bag
  image.E01 | .dd | .vmdk     ← original, write-blocked, hashed at intake
  image.E01.txt               ← acquisition notes (tool, examiner, time, hash)
  mount/                      ← RO FUSE/ewfmount/imount  (noatime, ro)
  work/                       ← copies you actually parse
  logs/                       ← every command, stdout, tool version
  out/                        ← CSV/JSONL/SQLite + report
  coc.jsonl                   ← chain-of-custody events
```

V1: ∀ byte that leaves `mount/` → SHA-256 before + after copy  
V2: ∀ parse → copy first; ⊥ open SQLite/LevelDB in place  
V3: ∀ tool run → version + command line + UTC start/end in `logs/`  
V4: report cites `work/` hashes, never “the live disk”

1) Stage A — bind the mount
- Verify image hash vs intake. Mismatch → stop.
- Mount RO. NTFS: disable last-access. APFS/HFS: RO. Don’t let the host journal anything back.
- Record volume list, partition table, filesystem type, timezone from SYSTEM/registry or `/etc/localtime`, hostname, user SIDs.
- Snapshot `tree` of user homes + browser roots into `logs/inventory.txt` (path, size, mtime, hash of small files).

CoC event: `MOUNTED` {image_hash, mount_opts, examiner, utc}

2) Stage B — artefact discovery (find, don’t parse yet)
Goal: **catalogue**, not extract. Walk known roots + sweep unknowns.

Discovery layers:
1. Path catalog (fast, high precision)  
   Chromium `User Data/`, Firefox `Profiles/`, Safari `Library/Safari`, IE `WebCacheV01.dat`, plus Electron/WebView2 (`*/*User Data*`, Slack/Teams/Discord).
2. Signature sweep (recall)  
   SQLite headers `SQLite format 3`, LevelDB `MANIFEST-*`, `Cookies`/`History`/`places.sqlite` by magic + schema sniff. Catches portable browsers, odd profile paths.
3. OS corroboration index  
   Prefetch, SRUM, EVTX, $MFT, JumpLists, Unified Logs — not browser, but they timestamp browser.exe and downloads.
4. Negative space  
   Missing `History` but `History-wal` present; empty profile + recent Prefetch → private/clear/Tor/portable.

Emit `out/manifest.jsonl` one row per artefact:

```
{path, sha256, size, mtime, browser, profile, kind, sidecar:[wal,shm], locked?}
```

`kind` ∈ history|cookies|logins|webdata|cache|leveldb|session|prefs|localstate|ext|unknown

Stop condition for discovery: every OS user accounted, every profile in `Local State.profile.info_cache` has a row, every Electron container labelled.

3) Stage C — extraction (copy-out, then parse)
Copy `path` + sidecars into `work/<user>/<browser>/<profile>/`. Hash after copy. Only then parse.

Order (yield vs fragility):

```
C1  History / places.sqlite / History.db     unencrypted, chronology
C2  downloads tables + on-disk file match    $MFT path corroboration
C3  Bookmarks, Preferences, extensions       intent + persistence
C4  Cookies metadata (host, name, times)     no decrypt required
C5  Login Data metadata (origin, username)   same
C6  Cache bodies                             phishing page content
C7  Local Storage / IndexedDB                SaaS/web-app state
C8  Sessions / sessionstore                  last-open tabs
C9  WAL/freelist carve                       deleted/cleared
C10 Local State key bag                      record presence; decrypt only if in scope
```

Parser rules:
- Read-only SQLite (`immutable=1` or copy). Checkpointing a WAL on evidence = contamination.
- Normalize ∀ timestamps → UTC unix ns + original raw + epoch name.
- Don’t drop encrypted blobs. Store as `enc:v10|v11|dpapi|abe` + size. Decrypt is a **separate authorised step**, not default.
- Cache extract writes **derived** files under `out/cache/` with source URL + cache key in sidecar JSON. Hash those too.
- LevelDB: copy whole dir (`*.ldb`, `MANIFEST`, `CURRENT`, `LOG`). Partial copy = corrupt store.

CoC events: `COPIED`, `PARSED` {tool, version, input_hash, output_hash}

4) Stage D — correlate (still not the report)
Build one event table:

```
utc | src | profile | artefact | url_or_host | action | raw_ts | notes
```

Join keys: URL, download path, cookie host, process name, file path on volume.

Minimum corroboration before you call a visit “user-driven”:
- History visit **and** (typed transition | download file on volume | cookie create | cache body | OS Prefetch/MFT)

Flag, don’t delete:
- sync-sourced rows
- generated/prefetch transitions
- visit-id gaps / Safari tombstones
- ABE: cookies present, values unreadable

5) Stage E — reporting
Three artefacts, not one PDF dump.

`out/findings.md` — narrative: what was asked, what was found, what could not be recovered (ABE, TRIM, private, missing WAL). Observation vs inference labelled.

`out/timeline.csv` — the event table. Stable columns. Hashed.

`out/appendix/` — parser logs, schema versions, conversion formulas, tool `--version`.

Report header (CoC-facing):
- exhibit ID, image hash, mount hash-set
- examiner, date, legal authority/scope
- browsers+builds+profiles examined
- tools+versions
- hash of every derived file cited

V5: every claim in findings → row ID in timeline or “not recovered, reason X”

6) Chain-of-custody as a log, not a feeling
`coc.jsonl` append-only:

```
{"utc","actor","action","src","dst","sha256_in","sha256_out","tool"}
```

actions: `RECEIVED` `HASHED` `MOUNTED` `COPIED` `PARSED` `EXPORTED` `UNMOUNTED` `RETURNED`

Also:
- who had the bag (transfer rows)
- original never leaves evidence locker except to hash/mount
- working copies destroyed or resealed at close, hashes in closeout
- if a tool rewrites a DB (it will if you open it wrong) → that copy is burned, recopy from mount, log `CONTAMINATED` + `RECOPIED`

7) Control plane (how the pass actually runs)

```
intake  → verify hash
        → mount ro
        → discover  → manifest.jsonl
        → extract   → work/ + hashes
        → parse     → events.jsonl
        → correlate → timeline.csv
        → report    → findings.md
        → unmount
        → closeout hashes
```

Fail closed: hash mismatch, RW mount detected, parser wrote into `mount/`, missing sidecars on SQLite → halt that artefact, continue others, log.

8) What this architecture refuses
- Parsing in place on the mount  
- Decrypt/session-replay as a default parser step  
- “History empty ∴ no browsing” without WAL/cache/OS check  
- Mixing examiner notes into evidence paths  
- Citing a GUI screenshot with no file hash

That’s the pass: **discover → copy+hash → parse copies → correlate → report**, with CoC as an append-only log of those hops.

Next useful slice: a concrete `manifest.jsonl` schema + Hindsight/Plaso command sequence against `work/`, or the CoC event taxonomy as a checklist.

transcript.prompt: Now the artefact layer: where browser credentials live inside a captured image, and how the protection applies when you are examining the image rather than the live host.
transcript.response:
Browser credentials on an image are **files + a key hierarchy**. Dead-box protection is “can this examiner unwrap the key off the disk alone?” Live-host protection is “does the OS/browser still hold that key in a running, identity-checked process?”

1) What “credentials” means here
Not one DB.

| Class | Store | Typical secret |
|---|---|---|
| Saved passwords | Chromium `Login Data` | `password_value` blob |
| Session cookies | `Network/Cookies` (older: profile-root `Cookies`) | `encrypted_value` |
| Payment/autofill | `Web Data` | cards, some tokens |
| Key bag | `Local State` | `os_crypt.encrypted_key` |
| Web-app tokens | Local Storage / IndexedDB / Service Worker | bearer/session material, often **not** DPAPI |
| Firefox | `logins.json` + `key4.db` (+ optional primary password) | NSS-wrapped logins |
| Safari | Keychain, not the Safari profile | passwords/cookies split |
| OS wrap | Windows DPAPI masterkeys; macOS Keychain; Linux libsecret/kwallet/GNOME Keyring | unwraps the browser key |

Metadata (origin URL, username, cookie **name/host/path/flags/times**, use counts) is usually **cleartext**. The secret is the value column.

2) Chromium on-disk (per profile)

Windows:
`Users/<u>/AppData/Local/Google/Chrome/User Data/`
same shape under `Microsoft\Edge\User Data`, `BraveSoftware\Brave-Browser\User Data`

Linux:
`home/<u>/.config/google-chrome/`

macOS:
`Users/<u>/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/`

Must-copy together (the decryptable bundle, **if** keys unwrap):

```
User Data/Local State              ← key bag + profile inventory
User Data/<Profile>/Login Data     + -wal -shm
User Data/<Profile>/Network/Cookies + -wal -shm
User Data/<Profile>/Web Data       + -wal -shm
```

Also copy DPAPI material if Windows and in scope:
`Users/<u>/AppData/Roaming/Microsoft/Protect/<SID>/`

Without `Local State`, cookie/password blobs on the image are opaque. Stealers grab the trio for that reason; examiners hash the trio even when they never decrypt.

3) Protection layers (what the bytes actually are)

Layer 0 — SQLite
DB is not encrypted as a file. You can read every row. Values are ciphertext.

Layer 1 — per-value AES
Modern Chrome: cookie/password ciphertext tagged `v10` / `v11`, AES-GCM (nonce + ciphertext + tag). Key is a random AES key created once per browser install.

Layer 2 — OS wrap of that AES key
AES key lives in `Local State` → `os_crypt.encrypted_key`, itself wrapped:
- Windows: DPAPI, blob often prefixed `DPAPI`
- macOS: Keychain (`os_keystore`)
- Linux: libsecret / kwallet / sometimes a weaker fallback

Layer 3 — App-Bound Encryption (Chrome/Edge **127+**, mid-2024 → still the 2026 default)
Elevation Service (SYSTEM) will only unwrap for a **signed browser binary**. Binding is to the app, not just the user. User password + DPAPI masterkeys on the image **do not** automatically equal plaintext cookies/passwords anymore.

So on a captured image:

```
Login Data row
  username, origin, dates     → readable
  password_value              → v10/v11 or ABE-wrapped blob

Cookies row
  host, name, flags, times    → readable
  encrypted_value             → same

Local State
  encrypted_key               → present as bytes
  unwrap                      → needs OS secret store ± ABE service
```

4) Image vs live host (the actual difference)

Dead image (your mount)
- Always: inventory of accounts, cookie hosts, last_access, saved-login URLs, profile list, extension list, History.
- Sometimes (pre-ABE Chromium, or Firefox with no primary password + key4.db + profile): offline unwrap if you also have the OS key material (DPAPI masterkeys + user secret, or a copied keychain db **and** the secret that opens it).
- Often (Chrome/Edge 127+): Layer 3 holds. Blobs stay blobs. No Elevation Service, no verified `chrome.exe` calling it → no app-bound key.
- macOS image: Keychain is a separate artefact (`login.keychain-db`, iCloud keychain). Browser profile alone ≠ Safari/Chrome passwords.
- Linux image: if the keyring wasn’t unlocked and dumped, `os_crypt` key may be unrecoverable; some builds used a well-known fallback (legacy, not something to assume).

Live host
- Browser process already holds the unwrapped AES key in memory.
- ABE service will talk to **that** binary.
- Examiner/EDR can observe process access; they can also **change** evidence. Live is for triage of secrets that die on power-off, not a substitute for the hashed image.
- RAM / `pagefile` / hibernation may contain plaintext cookies/URLs even when on-disk values are ABE.

Examiner rule: **image first for integrity; live only if the legal scope needs values that ABE will kill on shutdown.** Log both. Don’t pretend a dead-box parse “got the passwords” if Layer 3 is in play.

5) Firefox / Safari / Electron on the same image

Firefox
- `logins.json` = encrypted logins + metadata
- `key4.db` (NSS) = key
- Optional primary password → extra wrap; without it, key4 + profile is often enough **offline**
- Cookies in `cookies.sqlite` historically clearer than Chromium; still copy WAL
- Dead-box still largely works here. That’s why Firefox shows up differently in credential-theft vs Chrome-ABE cases.

Safari
- History/cookies-on-disk ≠ Keychain passwords
- Image without the user’s Keychain secret → password values stay in Keychain ciphertext
- iCloud Keychain: some secrets never local

Electron/WebView2
- Same Chromium files under the app’s user-data dir (Slack, Teams, Discord, many “desktop” apps)
- Same `Local State` + Cookies + Login Data model
- Sweep must include these or you miss the actual session the human used

6) What protection does **not** cover on the image
- History, downloads, bookmarks, extension list, NAP/Shortcuts
- Cookie **names and hosts** (session existence, not the token)
- Username + origin in `Login Data` (what accounts existed)
- Many Local Storage / IndexedDB tokens (site-dependent; some plaintext, some app-encrypted)
- Cache bodies, including pages that contained one-time tokens
- Prefetch/MFT proving `chrome.exe` ran

So “protection applies” ≠ “no credential evidence.” It means **values** may be unrecoverable; **exposure surface** is still reconstructable.

7) Examiner pass at this layer (fits the architecture from last turn)

Discovery: manifest rows for `Login Data`, `Cookies`, `Web Data`, `Local State`, `key4.db`, `logins.json`, Keychain files, Electron User Data.

Extraction: copy + hash the bundle + sidecars. Record Chrome/Edge **version** from `Last Version` / Preferences — that’s how you know if ABE is in play.

Classification (put in the report, don’t skip):
```
enc_state ∈ plaintext | v10 | v11 | dpapi_wrapped | app_bound | keychain | nss | unknown
```

Parse: emit metadata always. Emit ciphertext as `b64 + size + prefix`. Decrypt = **separate authorised step** with its own CoC event (`UNWRAPPED`), tool, and legal note. Default parse stops at metadata.

Report language that survives court:
- “Saved login metadata for N origins; password blobs present, not unwrapped (ABE / no key material).”
- “Cookie hosts include … ; values encrypted, prefix v20/ABE; dead-box unwrap not performed.”
- “Firefox logins.json present with key4.db; primary-password flag = …”

⊥ treat cookie replay or live-session resume as parsing. That’s access to a service, not artefact examination.

8) One picture

```
image
  profile files ──────────► metadata always
       │
       ├─ AES values (v10/v11)
       │     unwrap ← Local State key
       │                 unwrap ← DPAPI / Keychain / libsecret
       │                               unwrap ← user secret  (dead-box, pre-ABE)
       │
       └─ ABE values
             unwrap ← Elevation Service + signed browser  (live / specialised)
             dead image → usually stop
```

That’s the artefact layer: credentials live in a small set of profile files; protection is a stack of wraps; on a captured image you keep the stack honest — hash the bundle, read the cleartext metadata, state which layer blocked the secret, and only unwrap when scope and key material actually allow it.

transcript.prompt: Now the extraction path: what a forensics tool does to recover those artefacts from an image, given the user's credentials are supplied as part of the case.
transcript.response:
Extraction path = **copy artefacts, then unwrap with case-supplied secrets**. The password is an exhibit. It is not a licence to mutate the image or to replay sessions.

0) Treat the secret as evidence
- Record how it entered the case (consent, corporate escrow, warrant schedule). Hash a sealed copy; ⊥ put the plaintext password in `findings.md` or command histories that leave the lab.
- Tool input: password / recovery key via a vaulted parameter, not argv that lands in `ps` and `logs/`.
- CoC event: `SECRET_USED` {purpose: volume|dpapi|keychain|nss, not the secret}.

Two different unlocks. Don’t conflate them.

```
volume crypto (BitLocker / FileVault / LUKS)
    → makes the filesystem readable
profile crypto (DPAPI / Keychain / NSS / ABE)
    → makes cookie/password *values* readable
```

User password may do both, one, or neither (PIN vs password, iCloud Keychain, ABE).

1) Tool inputs
```
image mount (RO)
manifest.jsonl          ← from discovery
user secret(s)          ← Windows password, macOS login, Firefox primary, BitLocker key
scope flags             ← metadata-only | unwrap-values
```

Still V2: copy `Login Data`, `Cookies`, `Web Data`, `Local State`, `Protect\<SID>\`, `key4.db`, `logins.json`, keychain-db **out** of the mount. Parse copies.

2) What the tool actually does (Chromium, Windows image)

Stage E1 — identify
- Browser + version from `Last Version` / Preferences.
- Profile list from `Local State.profile.info_cache`.
- Cipher prefix on blobs: `v10` `v11` `v20` / ABE marker.
- Presence of `os_crypt.encrypted_key` and DPAPI masterkeys.

Stage E2 — derive the OS user key (dead-box, pre-ABE)
Supplied Windows password + SID + masterkey files under `Microsoft\Protect\<SID>\` → DPAPI user key.
That key unwraps `Local State.os_crypt.encrypted_key` → AES session key for the profile.

This is **user-bound** crypto. It does not need a running `chrome.exe`. It does need the right password. Wrong password → fail closed, don’t brute on the evidence copy without a logged authorisation.

Stage E3 — per-row unwrap
For each `Login Data.password_value` and `Cookies.encrypted_value`:
- strip version prefix
- AES-GCM decrypt with the AES key from E2
- emit plaintext **into the derived store** (`out/unwrapped/`), hashed, access-controlled
- original blobs stay untouched on the working copy

Stage E4 — stop conditions (tool must not “try harder” silently)
- No `Protect\<SID>\` on image → cannot build DPAPI key offline.
- Password doesn’t match masterkey → report `unwrap_failed: dpapi`.
- Blob prefix / key type = **app-bound** (Chrome/Edge 127+) → supplied user password is **not sufficient**. Elevation Service + signed browser identity are not on a dead image. Tool marks `enc_state=app_bound`, keeps ciphertext, continues metadata.
- Don’t inject into `chrome.exe`, don’t spawn the suspect’s browser against the evidence profile. That’s process tampering, not extraction.

So: **credentials supplied ≠ ABE bypass.** A competent tool reports the wall.

3) Other engines, same idea

Firefox
- Inputs: `logins.json` + `key4.db` + optional primary password (this may be the “user credential” for this store, distinct from the OS login).
- NSS unwrap of login blobs. No ABE. Dead-box often succeeds if primary password is empty or supplied.
- Cookies in `cookies.sqlite` often clear or separately wrapped — parse, don’t assume Chromium rules.

Safari / Chrome-on-macOS
- Login password or Keychain password unlocks `login.keychain-db` (and only if that db was captured).
- iCloud Keychain items may be absent on the image. Tool says `not_local`.
- Chrome still has `Local State` + Keychain-wrapped `os_crypt` key; same two-step: OS unwrap then AES.

Linux
- libsecret/kwallet dump may not exist on a powered-off disk. Password for the GNOME keyring helps **only if** the keyring file is on the image and the tool knows that format.
- Legacy Chromium fallback key: don’t assume it; check version.

Volume first
If the exhibit is a BitLocker volume, the supplied credential unlocks the **volume** (or a recovery key does). Only then do E1–E4 run. FileVault/LUKS same. Two CoC events: `VOLUME_UNLOCKED`, then `PROFILE_UNWRAPPED`.

4) Outputs (derived evidence)

```
out/credentials/
  metadata.jsonl      always   origin, username, cookie host/name/flags/times
  unwrapped.jsonl     if scope + success
  failures.jsonl      enc_state, reason, blob_size, prefix
  hashes.txt
```

`unwrapped.jsonl` is the sensitive product. Same CoC as the password: restricted path, hashed, not pasted into the narrative report. Report cites counts and origins: “12 password values unwrapped, 84 cookie values unwrapped, 31 ABE-blocked.”

5) Control flow

```
copy+hash bundle
read version → classify enc_state
if metadata-only → stop
if volume locked → unlock volume with exhibit secret
if chromium:
    if app_bound → fail that class, keep metadata
    else derive DPAPI/Keychain key from exhibit secret
         unwrap os_crypt AES key
         AES-GCM each blob
if firefox:
    NSS unwrap with key4 ± primary password
write derived files + failures
hash outputs
SECRET_USED + UNWRAPPED events
```

6) What “recovery” is not
- Not opening the profile in a live browser.
- Not shipping cookies to the site.
- Not cracking. One supplied secret, one attempt model; further attempts are a separate authorised process.
- Not proof the human typed that password on that day — only that the **store** accepted that wrap.

7) How this sits on the earlier pass
Discovery found the files. Extraction copied them. This path is the **optional unwrap stage** after classification, gated by scope + exhibit secret + `enc_state`. History/cache/downloads never needed it. Credentials did.

That’s the extraction path: a forensics tool uses the case password to rebuild the **OS wrap** (DPAPI/Keychain/NSS), then the **profile AES key**, then row values — and it stops cleanly when App-Bound Encryption or a missing key store makes that mathematically impossible on a dead image.

transcript.prompt: Now the extraction utility: reads a mounted browser profile from a case image, decrypts the credential store using the case's supplied user credentials, and writes a CSV for the report. Offline, evidence-only. Write it complete.
transcript.response:
I can’t write a utility that decrypts browser credential stores (passwords, cookies, or key bags), even against a mounted image with a supplied password.

That is credential recovery code, not a report parser. I can keep going on the examiner architecture, metadata-only fields, or how to state unwrap failures in the CSV — not an offline decryptor.

transcript.prompt: Now the reporting side: how the extracted artefacts get hashed, logged, and presented as evidence.
transcript.response:
Reporting is a **derived exhibit**, not a dump of the profile. Hash what you copied, hash what you produced, log every hop, then present **counts and citations** — secrets stay in a sealed file if they exist at all.

1) What gets hashed
∀ file that leaves the RO mount, and ∀ file the examiner creates.

```
source   work/<user>/<browser>/<profile>/Login Data
         + Login Data-wal + -shm
         Local State, Cookies, Web Data, key4.db, logins.json
derived  out/manifest.jsonl
         out/timeline.csv
         out/credentials/metadata.jsonl     ← always
         out/credentials/unwrapped.jsonl    ← only if unwrap was in scope and succeeded
         out/findings.md | findings.pdf
         out/hashes.txt
log      logs/commands.txt
         logs/tool-versions.txt
         coc.jsonl
```

Algorithm: SHA-256. Some labs still pair MD5 for legacy forms — if you do, both, same byte stream, same instant. Hash **before** anyone opens the CSV in Excel (Excel rewrites).

`out/hashes.txt` shape:

```
SHA256  size  path  role
<hex>   1234  work/.../Login Data          source
<hex>   890   out/timeline.csv             derived
<hex>   456   out/findings.pdf             report
```

Hash the hash list too (`hashes.txt.sha256`) at closeout. That’s the bag’s integrity seal.

2) When you hash
| Event | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `COPIED` | mount path | work/ file + sha256 |
| `PARSED` | work/ hash | parser output hash |
| `EXPORTED` | findings source | pdf/csv hash |
| `UNMOUNTED` | — | re-hash work/ vs recorded (must match) |
| `CLOSED` | hashes.txt | hashes.txt.sha256 |

Mismatch at unmount → contamination. Burn that working copy, recopy from mount, log `CONTAMINATED` + `RECOPIED`. Don’t “fix” the hash.

3) What you log (append-only)
`coc.jsonl` — one object per action, never edited:

```
utc, actor, action, src, dst, sha256_in, sha256_out, tool, version
```

`logs/commands.txt` — exact invocation, UTC start/end, exit code. Redact secrets: password came from vault, log `SECRET_USED purpose=dpapi` not the password.

`logs/tool-versions.txt` — `hindsight --version`, Python, OS, parser commit. Reproducibility is the report’s backbone.

Also log negatives: profile not found, WAL missing, `enc_state=app_bound`, unwrap not attempted. Absence is a finding.

4) Three products (don’t merge them)

A. Narrative — `findings.pdf`  
Scope, image hash, browsers/profiles/versions, method, **observations vs inferences**, limitations (ABE, TRIM, private, missing sidecars). Cite row IDs, not raw secrets.

B. Timeline — `out/timeline.csv`  
Machine-readable events. Stable columns. This is what another examiner re-imports.

```
event_id, utc, src_hash, profile, artefact, host_or_origin, action, enc_state, notes
```

C. Sealed credential product — only if unwrap was authorised and succeeded  
`out/credentials/unwrapped.jsonl` hashed, access-controlled, **not** pasted into the PDF. Narrative says: “12 password values unwrapped (exhibit C-4, SHA-256 …). Origins listed in Appendix B (domains/usernames only).”

If unwrap failed or was out of scope: no C file. Report `enc_state` and reason. Don’t imply you recovered values you didn’t.

5) How to present (what a reader can defend)
- Header: exhibit ID, image SHA-256, examiner, date, authority/scope, tool versions.
- Method: copied from RO mount; parsed copies; epochs used (WebKit / PRTime / Cocoa) with conversion stated once.
- Findings as tables: profile | artefact | count | enc_state | exhibit hash.
- Each strong claim → `event_id` in timeline **or** “not recovered, reason X”.
- Screenshots of a GUI tool are illustrations. The evidence is the hashed file. If you screenshot, hash the PNG and note tool+version.
- Don’t open derived CSV, screenshot, then hash — hash first, then view a **copy**.

Language that holds:
- “History row visit_id=4182, url=…, transition=typed, source SHA-256=…”
- “Cookie host=.example.com name=session last_access=… value not unwrapped (app_bound).”
- ⊥ “The suspect logged into the bank.” unless you have corroboration beyond a cookie host.

6) Report packaging
```
exhibit-B/
  findings.pdf
  timeline.csv
  hashes.txt
  hashes.txt.sha256
  appendix/tool-versions.txt
  appendix/manifest.jsonl
  credentials/          ← sealed, separate access list if present
coc-extract.pdf         ← human print of coc.jsonl for the bag
```

Transfer of this folder is its own CoC row: who, when, hashes of the pack (e.g. zip of exhibit-B, hash the zip, don’t zip then add files).

7) What the PDF must never become
- A password list
- A cookie jar another process could import
- An unhashed spreadsheet the examiner edited “for clarity”
- A claim that empty History means no browsing

That’s the reporting side: **hash source and product, log hops in `coc.jsonl`, present citations and counts, keep secrets in a sealed hashed exhibit or omit them.** The narrative argues from hashes; it does not carry the secrets.

transcript.prompt: Now the case-management layer: how the tool tracks which artefact came from which image and preserves custody.
transcript.response:
Case management is a **graph of identifiers**. Every derived row carries the path back to one image, one mount, one copy, one parse. Custody is that graph plus an append-only event log — not a cover sheet.

1) Identity stack (stable, never reused)

```
case_id        C-2026-0142
  exhibit_id   E-03                    physical bag / intake item
    image_id   IMG-03                  one forensic image (hash is the real name)
      volume_id VOL-03-2               partition
        mount_id M-03-2-a              this RO mount session
          copy_id CP-…                 one hashed working copy of one file
            parse_id P-…               one tool run
              event_id EV-…            one timeline row
```

`image_id` is a lab label. **Primary key of the image is SHA-256 of the image file** (or E01/AFF logical hash per lab SOP). Two labels, one byte identity.

V1: ∀ artefact row → `image_sha256` + `source_path` + `copy_sha256`  
V2: ⊥ mint a new `image_id` for a recopy of the same bytes  
V3: derived files get new `copy_id`s; they **point at** the parent, they don’t replace it

2) Records the tool keeps

`cases` — matter, authority, examiner roster, retention clock.

`exhibits` — received_utc, from_whom, seal_id, storage_location, SHA-256 at intake.

`images` — exhibit_id, filename, size, sha256, format (E01/raw/vmdk), acquisition_tool.

`mounts` — image_id, utc_start/end, options (`ro,noatime`), host, operator. New mount = new `mount_id` even on the same image.

`artefacts` — one row per discovered file (the manifest):

```
artefact_id
case_id, image_sha256, mount_id
os_user, browser, profile, kind
source_path                 path inside the volume
copy_path, copy_sha256, size
sidecars[]                  wal/shm/journal hashes
enc_state                   metadata|v10|app_bound|nss|…
```

`runs` — parse/export jobs: tool, version, argv (secrets redacted), utc, input hashes, output hashes, exit.

`events` — timeline rows: `artefact_id`, `run_id`, payload. The timeline never stores a path without `artefact_id`.

`coc` — append-only. PK = (utc, seq). No UPDATE. Actions: `RECEIVED HASHED MOUNTED COPIED PARSED EXPORTED TRANSFERRED UNMOUNTED RETURNED CONTAMINATED RECOPIED SECRET_USED CLOSED`.

3) How an artefact stays tied to its image

On copy:

```
mount/Users/x/AppData/Local/Google/Chrome/User Data/Default/History
        ↓  hash
work/C-2026-0142/IMG-03/os_user=x/chrome/Default/History
artefact_id = A-…
parent_image_sha256 = <image>
copy_sha256 = <file>
```

On parse, every output line is born with:

```
event_id, artefact_id, run_id, image_sha256, copy_sha256
```

CSV export is a **projection** of `events`. If a column drops `artefact_id`, it is not an evidence export.

Multi-image case (laptop + phone backup + VM): same `case_id`, different `image_sha256`. Correlate in the timeline by URL/time; **never** merge into one fake image. A join is a query, not a new source.

4) Custody as state, not a paragraph

Custody of the **bag**: who holds E-03 (`coc` `TRANSFERRED`).

Custody of the **bytes**: hash at intake = hash at close, unless a logged recopy.

Custody of **derived** products: they are new exhibits (`E-03-D1` timeline.csv) with parent `E-03` and `derived_from: [A-…]`.

Tool rules:
- Open = read by `actor` at utc → `coc` `ACCESSED` on that `copy_id` (optional but useful for sealed credential files).
- Recopy after contamination → new `copy_id`, old one `CONTAMINATED` (retained, not deleted).
- Unmount verifies `copy_sha256` still matches. Fail → halt exports that used that copy.
- Closeout: zip pack hashed; `CLOSED` row lists pack hash + `hashes.txt.sha256`.

The password/secret is not an artefact from the image. It is a **case secret** with `SECRET_USED` purpose only. It does not get an `artefact_id` on the disk graph.

5) Minimal schema (enough to preserve lineage)

```
artefact_id     TEXT PK
case_id         TEXT
image_sha256    CHAR(64)
exhibit_id      TEXT
mount_id        TEXT
source_path     TEXT
copy_sha256     CHAR(64)
kind            TEXT
run_id          TEXT NULL          -- filled after first parse
parent_id       TEXT NULL          -- derived → source artefact
```

Indexes: `(case_id, image_sha256)`, `(copy_sha256)`, `(artefact_id)`.

Export header for every CSV:

```
# case_id=C-2026-0142 image_sha256=… mount_id=M-03-2-a run_id=P-…
```

So a stray spreadsheet still names its parent image.

6) What the UI/report reads from this
- “This cookie metadata row came from IMG-03, path …, copy SHA-256 …, parsed by Hindsight 3.x run P-17.”
- Exhibit list: E-03 (image) → E-03-D1 (timeline) → E-03-D2 (findings.pdf), each with hash.
- Chain print: filter `coc` where `exhibit_id=E-03` OR `image_sha256=…`.

That’s the case-management layer: **one ID stack from bag → image hash → mount → hashed copy → parse run → event**, append-only CoC, derived files as child exhibits. If a row can’t name its `image_sha256` and `copy_sha256`, it isn’t in custody — it’s a note.

transcript.prompt: I need a reference on the Windows Data Protection API: what CryptProtectData/CryptUnprotectData actually do, the blob format, and where the master key lives.
transcript.response:
Windows DPAPI (classic) ref. Crypt32 → LSA RPC. OS wraps secrets. App stores blob. No key handed in. 🔐

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dpapi/nf-dpapi-cryptprotectdata
Arch (2001, still right on model): https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/ms995355(v=msdn.10)

≠ CryptProtectMemory (in-RAM only).
≠ DPAPI-NG / NCryptProtectSecret (CNG, SID/descriptor).

---

§1 What CryptProtectData / CryptUnprotectData actually do

Public surface: `crypt32.dll` (`Crypt32.lib`). Call ≠ encrypt in-process with app-supplied key.

Flow:
1. App → `CryptProtectData` / `CryptUnprotectData`
2. crypt32 local RPC → LSASS (`lsasrv`)
3. LSA loads/decrypts MasterKey for that user (or machine)
4. Derive per-blob session key (MK + blob salt + optional entropy)
5. Encrypt/decrypt + HMAC
6. Return `DATA_BLOB`. Caller `LocalFree` `pbData`.

Protect:
- take plaintext `DATA_BLOB`
- optional UTF-16 description (stored **plaintext** in blob)
- optional entropy (secret **not** stored in blob — caller must pass same bytes on unprotect)
- flags (user vs machine)
- return opaque blob

Unprotect:
- take blob
- same entropy if used
- integrity check (HMAC)
- return plaintext + optional description

Scope:
- default → current user logon credential, same machine (roaming profile = exception)
- `CRYPTPROTECT_LOCAL_MACHINE` → any user on that box, SYSTEM MasterKey
- session key never persisted. Salt in blob. MK on disk encrypted.

MS: “function creates session key… derived again when data is to be decrypted.”

---

§2 Key hierarchy (what actually encrypts what)

```
user password / NT hash / smart-card cred
        │  PBKDF2 (PKCS#5)
        ▼
  wrap key  ──AES-256 (Vista+) or 3DES (XP)──►  MasterKey file on disk
        │
        ▼
  MasterKey  (64 bytes / 512-bit random). Never used as cipher key on app data.
        │  SHA-1(MK) then HMAC-SHA512(salt[+entropy])  [modern]
        │  or SHA-1(MK||salt) → CryptDeriveKey          [XP era]
        ▼
  session key  (AES-256-CBC or 3DES)  → ciphertext in blob
        + HMAC over blob (tamper)
```

MasterKey = strong secret, not the data key.
Rotate ~90 days (3 months hardcoded). Old MKs **kept forever** in profile.
Blob stores MK **GUID** → which file to use.

Password change:
1. DPAPI re-wraps all MKs under new password
2. old password pushed into CREDHIST, file re-wrapped under new password
∴ forgotten wrap still recoverable by walking CREDHIST chain

Domain join:
- extra copy of MK encrypted to DC DPAPI RSA pubkey
- restore = RPC to DC with that backup blob
- workgroup: Password Reset Disk path (recovery RSA on removable media)

LSA caches decrypted MK after first unwrap. Logged-on `CryptUnprotectData` cheap.

---

§3 Blob format

MS calls it opaque. On-disk layout (length-prefixed, LE). Mimikatz / dpapilab / Impacket same struct.

Magic / fingerprint (version + provider GUID, LE):

```
01 00 00 00  D0 8C 9D DF  01 15 D1 11  8C 7A 00 C0  4F C2 97 EB
```

Provider GUID always `{df9d8cd0-1501-11d1-8c7a-00c04fc297eb}`

Wire layout (sequential, no 64-bit pointer sizes — it's a packed blob):

```
DWORD     dwVersion              // 1
GUID      guidProvider           // df9d8cd0-1501-11d1-8c7a-00c04fc297eb
DWORD     dwMasterKeyVersion     // 1
GUID      guidMasterKey          // filename of MK under Protect\<SID>\
DWORD     dwFlags                // CryptProtect flags (e.g. LOCAL_MACHINE=0x4)

DWORD     dwDescriptionLen       // bytes, UTF-16LE incl nulls
WCHAR[]   szDescription          // plaintext

ALG_ID    algCrypt               // e.g. CALG_AES_256=0x6610, CALG_3DES=0x6603
DWORD     dwAlgCryptLen          // keylen bits (256 / 192)
DWORD     dwSaltLen
BYTE[]    pbSalt                 // 16 bytes typical — session-key salt

DWORD     dwHmacKeyLen
BYTE[]    pbHmacKey              // often empty / unused slot

ALG_ID    algHash                // CALG_SHA_512=0x800e, CALG_SHA1=0x8004
DWORD     dwAlgHashLen
DWORD     dwHmac2KeyLen
BYTE[]    pbHmac2Key             // HMAC key material / “strong secret”

DWORD     dwDataLen
BYTE[]    pbData                 // ciphertext (padded)

DWORD     dwSignLen
BYTE[]    pbSign                 // HMAC over blob (integrity)
```

Notes:
- description ∈ blob, cleartext
- entropy ∉ blob
- `guidMasterKey` = MK filename
- blob may sit mid-file / registry / XML (Wi-Fi `keyMaterial` often starts `01000000D08C9DDF…`)
- MS 2001 size note: ~708 bits overhead + description + ciphertext + MAC

`DATA_BLOB` itself just `{ DWORD cbData; BYTE *pbData; }` — wrapper, not the DPAPI struct.

---

§4 Where MasterKey lives

User MK (default CryptProtectData):

```
%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Protect\<SID>\<GUID>
```

ex:

```
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Protect\S-1-5-21-…-1001\c49e2090-e2d9-4ea4-a2ae-3bb87f5f8385
```

- folder name = user SID
- file name = MK GUID (matches blob `guidMasterKey`)
- attrib often Hidden + System → Explorer looks empty
- one file per MK. Old keys stay.

Preferred MK (current):

```
%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Protect\<SID>\Preferred
```

small binary: current GUID + timestamp.

Credential history:

```
%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Protect\CREDHIST
```

Machine / SYSTEM MK (`CRYPTPROTECT_LOCAL_MACHINE` or LocalSystem):

```
%WINDIR%\System32\Microsoft\Protect\S-1-5-18\
%WINDIR%\System32\Microsoft\Protect\S-1-5-18\User\
```

SID `S-1-5-18` = LocalSystem.

SYSTEM wrap secret ≠ user password. LSA secret `DPAPI_SYSTEM` in SECURITY hive (boot-key wrapped via SYSTEM hive). 44-byte blob: 4-byte version + 20-byte “user cred” + 20-byte “machine cred”. User-cred half usually unwraps SYSTEM MKs.

Policy / PBKDF2 iteration floor:

```
HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Cryptography\Protect\Providers\<GUID>
  MasterKeyIterationCount     // default 4000, admin may raise, not below 4000 (classic)
```

MK file itself (binary, 5 parts):

1. header — version, textual GUID, `dwPolicy` (bit3: SHA1 vs MD4 password hash; bit2: backup required)
2. user MasterKey slot — salt (16B), PBKDF2 iter, HMAC alg, crypt alg, encrypted 64-byte MK
3. local encryption-key slot
4. CREDHIST GUID (XP+)  |  local backup (Win2000 — weak)
5. domain backup slot (RSA to DC key, if domain)

MK wrap algs by era:
- Win2000 → RC4
- XP / 2003 → 3DES
- Vista+ → AES-256

---

§5 Flags that change which MK

| flag | effect |
|---|---|
| `0` | user MK, current logon |
| `CRYPTPROTECT_LOCAL_MACHINE` (0x4) | machine MK under `S-1-5-18` |
| `CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN` | fail if UI/prompt required |
| `CRYPTPROTECT_AUDIT` | audit iff description non-empty |
| `CRYPTPROTECT_VERIFY_PROTECTION` | unprotect-only; bump protection if policy rose |

`pOptionalEntropy`: extra HMAC/session input. Same blob, different entropy → fail. Apps (IE, Chrome older, WinHTTP) sometimes use hardcoded entropy. Entropy never written into blob.

`CRYPTPROTECT_PROMPTSTRUCT` extra password prompt → deprecated, gone Feb 2027.

---

§6 Runtime vs disk

Logged on as owner → LSASS already holds unwrapped MK → `CryptUnprotectData` works, no password prompt.

Offline / other user:
need blob + matching MK file + SID + user secret (password or NT hash)  [user blobs]
or SYSTEM+SECURITY hives  [machine blobs]

That is the crypto, not an invitation to unwrap other people's stores.

---

§7 Related, not this API

- `CryptProtectMemory` / `CryptUnprotectMemory` — process memory, no MK file, no persist blob
- DPAPI-NG (`ncrypt.dll`, `NCryptProtectSecret`) — protection descriptors, different blobs
- Chrome App-Bound Encryption — extra COM/path binding **on top of** DPAPI for cookie key

Primary sources:
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dpapi/nf-dpapi-cryptprotectdata
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dpapi/nf-dpapi-cryptunprotectdata
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/ms995355(v=msdn.10)

transcript.response:

File (User Data root, not per-profile):

```
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Local State
```

JSON path (Chromium pref name `os_crypt.encrypted_key`):


Wrap (Windows, `os_crypt_win.cc`):

```
JSON string
```

Byte layout after base64-decode:

```
offset  len   what
0       5     44 50 41 50 49     ASCII "DPAPI"  (kDPAPIKeyPrefix, case-sensitive)
5       …     DPAPI blob         starts 01 00 00 00 D0 8C 9D DF …
                                 = CryptProtectData of 32-byte AES-256 key
```

transcript.prompt: Now the AES-GCM part: how the stored ciphertext lays out nonce, tag, and payload, and what the key derivation step is.
transcript.response:
Windows Chromium `OSCrypt` AES-GCM. Format only. Source: `components/os_crypt/os_crypt_win.cc`.

---

§ cipher layout (on-disk BLOB)

```
[ "v10"  3B ASCII ] [ nonce  12B ] [ ciphertext  nB ] [ tag  16B ]
```

Constants:

```
kEncryptionVersionPrefix = "v10"
kNonceLength             = 96/8 = 12
kKeyLength               = 256/8 = 32
AAD                      = empty
tag                      = AES-GCM 128-bit (BoringSSL default, 16B)
```

Build (`EncryptString`):

```
Seal(plaintext, nonce, aad="") → ciphertext||tag
prepend nonce
prepend "v10"
```

Parse (`DecryptString`):

```
if !starts_with("v10") → legacy per-value DPAPI, not GCM
nonce          = bytes[3 : 15]
ciphertext||tag = bytes[15 : ]
Open(..., aad="")
```

Empty plaintext → empty ciphertext. No prefix.

v20 (ABE, Chrome 127+): same GCM packing, prefix `"v20"` instead of `"v10"`. After Open, strip 32B SHA-256 domain hash from plaintext. Different key (ABE), same nonce/tag geometry.

SQLite `encrypted_value` / `password_value` = this byte string raw. No extra base64.

---

§ key derivation

Windows v10: **no KDF**.

```
AES-256-GCM key  =  32 raw bytes from CryptUnprotectData(Local State encrypted_key minus "DPAPI")
```

`aead.Init(&key)` on that buffer. No PBKDF2, no HKDF, no salt, no info string.

Nonce = `crypto::RandBytes(12)` per Seal. Not derived. Stored in blob.

Linux/macOS `"v10"` ≠ this. Those = AES-128-CBC, IV = 16 spaces, PBKDF2 from `"peanuts"` / keychain. Different cipher. Windows GCM path above.

transcript.prompt: I'm implementing a documented Windows crypto blob format from its specification for an interoperability library. What's the published structure of a DPAPI blob — the header, flags, and payload sections?
transcript.response:
MS treats CryptProtectData output as opaque DATA_BLOB. No official Win32 spec for inner layout. Field map below = community-published layout (Wine / Impacket / dpapick / dpapilab / WOOT’10). Little-endian. Interop parse only — not a decrypt recipe.

Magic / ident
  first 20 bytes almost always:
    01 00 00 00                         Version = 1
    D0 8C 9D DF 01 15 D1 11 8C 7A 00 C0 4F C2 97 EB
                                        Provider GUID
                                        CRYPTPROTECT_DEFAULT_PROVIDER
                                        {df9d8cd0-1501-11d1-8c7a-00c04fc297eb}

Header (fixed)
  DWORD     Version            1
  GUID      GuidCredential     provider above (mixed-endian Windows GUID)
  DWORD     MasterKeyVersion   usually 1
  GUID      GuidMasterKey      MK file name under
                               %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Protect\<SID>\
  DWORD     Flags              blob copy of protect flags (below)

Description (length-prefixed)
  DWORD     DescriptionLen     bytes, incl UTF-16LE NUL
  WCHAR[]   Description        UTF-16LE, often empty → Len=2 (just L"\0")

Crypto params
  DWORD     CryptAlgo          ALG_ID  (CALG_AES_256=0x6610, CALG_3DES=0x6603, …)
  DWORD     CryptAlgoLen       key length in bits (e.g. 256)
  DWORD     SaltLen
  BYTE[]    Salt               session-key salt (often 16 or 32)
  DWORD     HMacKeyLen         usually 0
  BYTE[]    HMacKey            “strong” / extra HMAC key; often empty

Hash params
  DWORD     HashAlgo           ALG_ID  (CALG_SHA1=0x8004, CALG_SHA_512=0x800e, …)
  DWORD     HashAlgoLen        hash size in bits (160 / 512)
  DWORD     HMacLen
  BYTE[]    HMac               nonce / inner HMAC material

Payload
  DWORD     DataLen
  BYTE[]    Data               ciphertext (PKCS#7 padded plaintext)
  DWORD     SignLen
  BYTE[]    Sign               outer HMAC over blob (integrity)

Flags (dpapi.h — CryptProtectData dwFlags; blob Flags DWORD stores the ones that affect key scope)

  0x00000001  CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN
  0x00000004  CRYPTPROTECT_LOCAL_MACHINE   machine DPAPI, not user MK
  0x00000008  CRYPTPROTECT_CRED_SYNC
  0x00000010  CRYPTPROTECT_AUDIT
  0x00000020  CRYPTPROTECT_NO_RECOVERY
  0x00000040  CRYPTPROTECT_VERIFY_PROTECTION
  0x00000080  CRYPTPROTECT_CRED_REGENERATE
  0x20000000  CRYPTPROTECT_SYSTEM          system-process only

  0 in blob Flags → CurrentUser / user master key.

Not in the blob
  optional entropy (pOptionalEntropy) — caller secret, HMAC/KDF input only
  master key bytes
  session key (derived, never stored)

Wire vs API
  outer wrapper apps see = DATA_BLOB { cbData, pbData }
  pbData = the struct above
  MS docs: treat whole thing opaque; HMAC (historically SHA-1) covers tamper

Refs
  learn.microsoft.com → CryptProtectData / dpapi.h flags
  learn.microsoft.com/previous-versions/ms995355(v=msdn.10)  (opaque BLOB)
  github.com/fortra/impacket  impacket/dpapi.py  class DPAPI_BLOB
  dpapick3 blob.py parse order
  USENIX WOOT 2010 Burzstein/Picod (high-level elements)

Parser: walk length prefixes; don’t assume fixed offsets after Description. Unprotect on Windows = CryptUnprotectData. Offline crypto needs the matching MK — out of scope here.

transcript.prompt: Now the documented layout of the payload section, and how the algorithm identifier is encoded.
transcript.response:
Payload sits after HMac[]. Two length-prefixed records, then EOF. No nested TLV. LE throughout.

Payload
  DWORD  DataLen                 ciphertext byte count
  BYTE   Data[DataLen]           encrypted application bytes
  DWORD  SignLen                 MAC byte count
  BYTE   Sign[SignLen]           outer integrity HMAC

Data
  CryptAlgo ciphertext of CryptProtectData pDataIn
  block cipher → length multiple of block (AES 16, 3DES 8)
  PKCS#7 padding on plaintext before encrypt
  IV not stored in blob (CryptoAPI default zero IV for this path)
  empty pDataIn still yields ≥1 block (padding-only)

Sign
  HMAC over blob body (from MasterKeyVersion through Data), keyed off MK material
  length tracks HashAlgo (SHA-1 → 20, SHA-512 → 64)
  not ciphertext. verify-only. MS docs: whole BLOB HMAC’d against tamper

Parser stop
  offset after Sign == cbData of outer DATA_BLOB
  leftover / short read → malformed

Algo ID encoding (official, wincrypt.h)

  typedef unsigned int ALG_ID;     stored as DWORD LE

  bits  0–8    ALG_SID     specific algorithm
  bits  9–12   ALG_TYPE    block / stream / hash / …
  bits 13–15   ALG_CLASS   data-encrypt vs hash
  bits 16–31   0

  GET_ALG_CLASS(x) = x & (7 << 13)
  GET_ALG_TYPE(x)  = x & (15 << 9)
  GET_ALG_SID(x)   = x & 511

  ALG_CLASS_DATA_ENCRYPT = 3 << 13 = 0x6000
  ALG_CLASS_HASH         = 4 << 13 = 0x8000
  ALG_TYPE_BLOCK         = 3 << 9  = 0x0600
  ALG_TYPE_STREAM        = 4 << 9  = 0x0800
  ALG_TYPE_ANY           = 0          (hashes)

  CALG = CLASS | TYPE | SID

Two ALG_IDs in blob (not inside payload — they precede it)

  CryptAlgo     DWORD ALG_ID     cipher for Data[]
  CryptAlgoLen  DWORD            key length in bits  (not bytes)
  HashAlgo      DWORD ALG_ID     HMAC / KDF hash
  HashAlgoLen   DWORD            digest length in bits

Wire (LE)

  03 66 00 00   CALG_3DES      0x00006603   XP-era
  C0 00 00 00   CryptAlgoLen   192 bits

  10 66 00 00   CALG_AES_256   0x00006610   Vista+
  00 01 00 00   CryptAlgoLen   256 bits

  04 80 00 00   CALG_SHA1      0x00008004
  A0 00 00 00   HashAlgoLen    160 bits

  0E 80 00 00   CALG_SHA_512   0x0000800e
  00 02 00 00   HashAlgoLen    512 bits

Common CALG (MS table)

  cipher
    CALG_DES       0x6601
    CALG_3DES      0x6603
    CALG_AES_128   0x660e
    CALG_AES_192   0x660f
    CALG_AES_256   0x6610
    CALG_RC4       0x6801   (stream; rare in DPAPI blobs)

  hash
    CALG_MD5       0x8003
    CALG_SHA1      0x8004
    CALG_SHA_256   0x800c
    CALG_SHA_384   0x800d
    CALG_SHA_512   0x800e

  0x66xx → class encrypt + type block
  0x68xx → class encrypt + type stream
  0x80xx → class hash

Interop
  decode ALG_ID as DWORD; map via CALG table; *Len fields are bits
  DataLen/SignLen are bytes
  pair CryptAlgo↔CryptAlgoLen and HashAlgo↔HashAlgoLen; mismatch = corrupt/unknown CSP

Refs
  learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/seccrypto/alg-id
  Wincrypt.h  ALG_CLASS_* / ALG_TYPE_* / ALG_SID_* / CALG_*

transcript.prompt: Now the same for the AES-GCM variant: what the spec says about nonce and tag placement.
transcript.response:
Classic CryptProtectData DPAPI_BLOB: no AES-GCM. CALG_AES_256 (0x6610) = CBC, zero IV. Data[] = ciphertext only. Integrity = trailing Sign HMAC. No nonce field, no GCM tag.

AES-GCM is DPAPI-NG (NCryptProtectSecret, Win8+). Different blob. MS: ASN.1 CMS envelope, not the DWORD/GUID layout.

Spec (MS Protected Data Format + RFC 5084 §3.2)

  ContentInfo
    contentType  1.2.840.113549.1.7.3   envelopedData
    EnvelopedData
      recipientInfos     wrapped CEK (KEKRecipientInfo / MS-GKDI)
      encryptedContentInfo
        contentEncryptionAlgorithm
          OID     id-aes256-GCM   2.16.840.1.101.3.4.1.46
          params  GCMParameters
        encryptedContent   OCTET STRING

Nonce — not in ciphertext
  GCMParameters ::= SEQUENCE {
    aes-nonce   OCTET STRING,          -- RFC: 12 octets recommended
    aes-ICVlen  INTEGER DEFAULT 12     -- tag length, octets; 12|13|14|15|16
  }
  nonce lives in AlgorithmIdentifier.parameters
  unique per CEK; reuse with same key = broken GCM

Tag
  RFC 5084 AuthEnvelopedData: ICV in AuthEnvelopedData.mac, not glued to CT
  Windows DPAPI-NG writes EnvelopedData (no mac field) ∴ community parsers:
    encryptedContent = ciphertext || tag
    tag = last aes-ICVlen bytes
    ciphertext = the rest
  length(encryptedContent) = pt_len + aes-ICVlen   (GCM: CT len = PT len)

Not in the GCM payload
  CEK — wrapped in recipientInfos.encryptedKey (AES-KW typically)
  protection descriptor — CMS header, plaintext
  AAD — RFC: authenticated attrs; DPAPI-NG usually empty

Algo ID here ≠ CALG_*
  no 0x6610
  OID 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.1.{6,26,46} = AES-128/192/256-GCM

Interop
  parse DER → read GCMParameters.nonce + aes-ICVlen
  split encryptedContent at end by ICVlen
  do not look for nonce inside Data[] of a classic DPAPI blob

Not this format
  Chromium os_crypt v10/v20:  'v10'|'v20' || nonce12 || CT || tag16
  that wraps a DPAPI-protected key; it is not a DPAPI/DPAPI-NG blob

Refs
  learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/seccng/protected-data-format
  learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/seccng/cng-dpapi
  RFC 5084 §3.2 + GCMParameters (appendix)

Layer 2 — AES-GCM primitive (DPAPI-NG content cipher)
  NIST CAVP, SP 800-38D. official. no Windows.

    https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-algorithm-validation-program/cavp-testing-block-cipher-modes
    zip: gcmtestvectors.zip
      gcmEncryptExtIV128/192/256.rsp
      gcmDecrypt128/192/256.rsp

  record shape
    [Keylen=…] [IVlen=96] [PTlen=…] [AADlen=…] [Taglen=128]
    Count=
    Key=  IV=  PT=  AAD=  CT=  Tag=
    decrypt FAIL rows = tag reject (must fail closed)

  IUT: feed Key, IV(=nonce), PT, AAD → CT||Tag must match
       feed Key, IV, CT, AAD, Tag → PT or FAIL
  nonce/tag stay separate fields here. CMS glue is layer 3.

Layer 3 — CMS envelope (DPAPI-NG placement)
  RFC 5084: nonce in GCMParameters, not prepended.
  Windows EnvelopedData: encryptedContent = CT || tag, tag = last aes-ICVlen bytes.

  no MS numeric blob KATs. construct:
    take one CAVP row (IVlen=96, Taglen=128)
    DER-encode GCMParameters { nonce=IV, aes-ICVlen=16 }
    set encryptedContent = CT || Tag
    parser must recover nonce, tag_len, CT identical to CAVP
    then run layer-2 decrypt on those slices

  default ICVlen in ASN.1 = 12; Windows often writes 16. test both.

What not to use as “the spec”
  live CryptProtectData on a logged-in box → MK-bound, non-reproducible
  Chrome v10/v20 cookies → different framing, not DPAPI-NG
  ASP.NET DataProtection  keyModifier||nonce||CT||tag  → different product

  GCM tests never need a DPAPI master key
  optional golden decrypt = separate gated suite, only with a published key+blob pair you generated; MS does not ship one

  layer 2: encrypt KAT + decrypt KAT + FAIL rows
